root_cause.text: Failure to zero-initialize the entire `struct iw_point` local variable before filling its fields, leaving a 32-bit padding hole on 64-bit architectures uninitialized, which leaks kernel stack memory to user space.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states "struct iw_point has a 32bit hole on 64bit arches" and that the patch "Make sure to zero the structure to avoid disclosing 32bits of kernel data." The patch adds `memset(&iwp, 0, sizeof(iwp))` in both `compat_standard_call()` and `compat_private_call()` to eliminate the uninitialized padding.

bic_trace_step.reason: In `compat_private_call`, `struct iw_point iwp;` is declared without zero-initialization, then fields `iwp.pointer`, `iwp.length`, `iwp.flags` are assigned individually. This leaves the 32-bit padding hole on 64-bit architectures uninitialized, which can leak kernel stack memory to user space when the struct is copied out.
